title: The brief before the brief.
metaDesc: Why the most important part of a project happens before anyone opens a Figma file.

texts.text: Why the most important part of a project happens before anyone opens a Figma file.

The most important part of any Mira project happens before anyone opens a design file. Here is why the discovery call, not the brief document, is where the real work of a project actually gets defined, and what we listen for in the first thirty minutes that reshapes the whole engagement.

Clients usually come to a studio with a specific request. A rebrand. A website redesign. A packaging refresh. Those requests are almost never wrong, but they are almost never the whole problem either. They are the surface symptom of something bigger sitting underneath.

texts.text: Scope creep happens when the definition of the project changes after work has started. What we are describing is the opposite: doing the definition properly before work starts, so no one is surprised later. That work is unglamorous. It happens on a Zoom call, not in Figma. It is also the single biggest predictor of whether a project ships well.
